## Maintainer ruling — ADR-0150 open questions Q1 and Q2 · 2026-11-08T16:31Z

⛔ Not a claim. Ruling-ref: decision card cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XX2ScaRkjtxxoSRmu1t8H2p. The maintainer tapped **option 0 「A+A，含对象动作补充」** at 2026-11-08T16:30:25Z. The tap record cannot be attached, so the card id and time are the reference.

- **Q1 = A, with the object-action refinement.** A bucket-3 item's AI/MCP face name is `NS-NAME`: the namespace, a hyphen, then the name. Past 64 characters it is cut to 55, then a hyphen and 8 hex characters of a hash of the full identity are appended. **An object-bound action spells `OBJECT-ACTION`** (for example `crm_lead-convert_lead`): one package may bind the same action name to several objects (the #5510 dedup reading), and the object name already carries the global prefix. Object-less actions, and tool, skill, agent and rag_pipeline, use `NS-NAME`. The cloud action tool (#31515) derives its name from the same function.
- **Q2 = A.** A position name that two packages ship keeps the one-holder refusal. An administrator binds another package's permission set to a position through an ADR-0005 overlay of that position. No merge engine.
- **Unblocked:** child P (face derivation), G2 (MCP face names), and cloud #31515.
- **Still with the maintainer:** ADR-0150 D2, uniqueness of behavioural names across a namespace's co-owners, which is child N.

ADR-0150 (#31586) is being amended to record both answers as decided.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1** — number 0150 because 0149 is taken by #31535: 0149 is on `main` (`0149-ai-answers-business-questions-…`), index regenerated after the merge of `origin/main`. Answered.
- **Dev deviation 2** — child N and the 13 trailing B children added beyond the evaluation's 18–22: N is judged in ④ (S6); the B children follow red line 3 and are right. The count sentence is off by one (④ N5).
- **`open_questions` Q1 (face spelling) and Q2 (position conflicts)** — both `needs_decision` for the maintainer; the card body names exactly these two as "this card's decision". Correctly escalated, not answered here. The record must not presume them anywhere: it does in two places (④ S4).
- **Dev out-of-scope note** — "a package whose namespace is literally `global` would make `/actions/global/...` read as object-less first … recorded rather than gated": recorded on the PR body only, not in the tree. The tree is judged, so this is ④ S2.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the card's three red lines, the three rulings, the first consumer (child R #31575, filed 2026-11-08T15:49Z) and the execution plan. **No must-fix.** Six should-fix, five nits.

**docs/adr/0150 — the design (D1–D10):** D1's buckets restate ruling 6723462584 faithfully, including the exceptions, and the "why objects differ" answer is correct against ADR-0129 D2 (the object name is the table name and leaves the platform). D3 is the ruled rule verbatim and reuses `bare-name-one-holder.ts`'s vocabulary, which exists as cited. D4's "today" column matches the readers as they are (flow map by name, action `objectName:name`, ledger `(metadata_type, name)`, webhooks/queues first match, `jobKeyFor`). D8 adds columns beside names (ADR-0126 §4) and leaves the ambiguous set null and reported — red line 2 holds. D10 holds. Q1's four-axis table is sound on the provider constraints and the regexes. Q2's recommendation is sound against `security-catalog-namespace.ts`. The findings:

- **S1 (should-fix) — the plan's releasability premise and its Narrowing arms are wrong for the twelve types phase 1 does not cover.** The plan says "while phase 1's refusal stands, no two package holders of a name exist, so adding the coordinate changes no observable answer", and G1 declares "no: a bare address that resolves today still resolves". That is true for the 12 `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` and permission sets. For sharing rule, queue, assignment rule, hook, job, app, page, dashboard, report, book, cube and tool there is no backstop: two unrelated packages may hold `page/home` today, and the bare read serves the first match (`registry.ts` `getItem` with no package iterates the Map; `ownership-queue-service.ts` `declaredItems().find`; ADR-0048 §3.3 "best-effort, first match" stands for packages with no dependency relation). After E4/E6/E8 and G1 that same bare read answers a refusal / `409`. That is the right outcome (red line 2 beats silence) but it is a **narrowing**, and proof (b) "bare-name behaviour unchanged" cannot be met for those types on a deployment that already holds two. Fix, one paragraph: say that for the uncovered types the switch converts a silent first match into a reported refusal, declare E4/E6/E8/G1 `Narrowing: yes for a today-ambiguous bare name of an uncovered type (measured first-party: 0)`, and scope proof (b) to names with one holder — or, the design alternative, widen N to a one-holder-per-environment backstop for those types first so red line 3 holds literally.
- **S2 (should-fix) — D5's router precedence leaves two cases unaddressed.** (a) D2 gives the environment package no namespace and no address, so an environment-authored flow whose bare name equals an installed namespace (or a namespace installed later over an existing environment name) loses every sub-resource door (`/automation/NAME/runs`, `/trigger`, `/toggle`, `/clone`) with no qualified address to fall back to; "still reachable by its qualified address" holds for package items only. (b) The grammar's literal segments — `trigger`, `hooks`, `connectors`, `global`, `_status`, `_activation`, `types`, `_drafts` — are not reserved: `RESERVED_NAMESPACES` is `{base, system}` plus `sys` (`registry.ts:435`, `:2367`), and `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$` admits `trigger`, `hooks`, `global`. Read literally, "a first segment that names an installed namespace is the namespace" lets a package named `trigger` take `/automation/trigger/:name`. Fix, two sentences in D5: the grammar's literals are read before a namespace and a namespace spelling one is refused at install (ADR-0048 §3.2's reserved set grows by them — a narrowing to declare); and the environment package gets a spelled address segment, or an environment item may not take an installed namespace as its bare name (refused at the save door and `os validate`, naming the namespace).
- **S3 (should-fix) — D4's overlay row and D8's R15 do not say what a package-less `sys_metadata` row bearing a package-held name is.** R15 says overlays "already carry the package"; `sys-metadata.object.ts` says "a package-less / global overlay uses NULL", `registerItem` hydrates that row into the bare slot with no `packageId`, and ADR-0146 D8 item 1 names "a stored row with no package — the row Setup writes today" as a live shape that D11 migrates. Today that row is the ADR-0005 overlay of whichever package holds the name (and `bare-name-one-holder.ts` says it is never a holder). Under D2 a package-less row is a bucket-4 environment item; under D3 "the environment item of that name first" and under E1 "all same-named flows arm", so the row that shadows `crm/send_email` today would arm beside it tomorrow — an observable change red line 3 forbids — and the ruling's "409 when not unique in the environment" and D3's "environment item first" then disagree on the same two holders. Fix: state in D4 that a package-less row bearing a package-held name is the customization of the one phase-1 holder and never a second item; add an R15 backfill row (bind `package_id` to that holder; two holders → the ambiguous set, reported) or cite ADR-0146 D11 as the owner; and say a bucket-4 item cannot take a package-held name of its type.
- **S4 (should-fix) — Q2 is presumed in two places.** The ADR-0048 status line this PR adds says the one-holder refusal "stays for platform-requested bare names and positions"; positions are Q2. D7's closing paragraph ("A package that needs its permission sets on another package's position asks the environment to bind them … A merge is ruled by its own card") reads as decided, and only holds under option A. Fix: "and, pending Q2, positions" on ADR-0048; "Under the recommended option," opening D7's paragraph. (D8 R2's "none" is fine: environment-scoping is ruled, independent of Q2.)
- **S5 (should-fix) — the status line's gate is already false.** "⛔ the cards under Execution plan are cut after that merge, never before it" — child R is #31575, filed 2026-11-08T15:49:53Z under the epic ruling 6723499113 and the division-of-labour ruling 6723571682 (which runs R beside the ADR's review at concurrency 2), and the card body lists all seven children. Fix: "child cards are filed under the epic ruling 6723499113; no child lands before this record is accepted".
- **S6 (should-fix) — child N is a new refusal the three rulings did not name, and the record does not say so.** The ruling's address example `/automation/crm/send_email` is a namespace, five HotCRM packages co-own `crm`, so a qualified address needs either N (refuse a second co-owner holder at install and `os validate`) or a `409` on the qualified address with package-id candidates (`?package=` already disambiguates `/meta`). The ADR picks N in D2 and marks it `Narrowing: yes`, but D6 applies the startup rule "a new gate defaults to no" to Q1's options while N, the one gate this record adds, is not put to the maintainer and the alternative is absent from Alternatives. Fix: name N in the TL;DR as the one refusal added beyond the rulings and either list it as Q3 or add the rejected alternative with its reason.

- **N1 (nit)** — D6/Q1: "parses back to (namespace, name) with no lookup table" fails for the hashed long form (`…-` plus 8 hex introduces a second hyphen); say "except the hashed form, which the registry resolves".
- **N2 (nit)** — ADR-0150 has no `**Supersedes**:` field line, so `scripts/adr-index.mjs` leaves its Supersedes cell `—` while ADR-0028's Superseded-by cell names ADR-0150; add the field line (`ADR-0028 in part`) and regenerate.
- **N3 (nit)** — D3 says the closure is "manifest.dependencies, transitively, plus `sys`"; `resolvePackageClosure` (`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:591`) adds no `sys` and ADR-0141 TL;DR 2 admits "platform objects" by a separate clause. Right design, but R's row should say the resolver adds `sys` itself.
- **N4 (nit)** — D9 and child U cite "ADR-0146 D3's prefix on a Studio-authored non-object name"; ADR-0146 D3 prefixes object names only (`crm_custom_SHORT`) and says nothing about non-object names. Cite the real source (#30805's Studio text, if any) or drop the clause.
- **N5 (nit)** — "D, R, N, P, A, U, C, 8 E, 3 G and 4 S make 21 build children" is 22 (7 + 8 + 3 + 4); correct the count or the critical-path sentence that leans on it.

**docs/adr/0048 — status line:** right except S4 (positions presumed). **docs/adr/0028 — status line:** right; D2 stays Deferred, the re-open trigger is answered by the ruling, nothing else moves. **docs/adr/README.md:** generated by `pnpm adr:index`, `Lint · docs & code guards` is green on the head; right (N2 is a source-side nit, not an index defect).

**Execution-plan order** (R before N/E/G, N before G1, S after E and G, B per type last, A trailing) keeps every intermediate `main` releasable for the 13 covered types; for the 12 uncovered types see S1. Nothing in the plan cuts a slice that depends on Q1 before it is ruled (P's face derivation, G2's face names, C are gated on Q1). Q2 blocks nothing. The first consumer, #31575, matches D3's arms (own package → unique closure holder → refusal with candidates; context-free caller → unique environment holder → `409`) and adds no reader — consistent with the R row.

- **Q1, Q2** — `status: decided`, with the card option, time and record; D6/D7 carry the same. Answered by ruling, recorded.
- **D2 / child N** — pending the maintainer's word, as the ruling left it ("Still with the maintainer"); marked ⛔ in TL;DR 7, D2, the N row, Consequences and the critical path. Correctly escalated, not presumed anywhere.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the delta and the full ADR against the three rulings plus `6724050556`, the first consumer (#31575) and the execution plan. **No must-fix.** Four should-fix, four nits.

- **S7 (should-fix) — the covered/uncovered partition behind the new narrowing declarations is wrong against the constant it cites.** `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` (`bare-name-one-holder.ts:169`) is picklist, mapping, dataset, api, action, function, flow, webhook, connector, email_template, agent, skill.
